subject: BlueProxy: request for subprocessor roster & transit details
messages:
From: Diana Lopez <diana.lopez@blueproxy.io>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: BlueProxy subprocessor roster and transit details

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the time last week. As part of our security onboarding we need a current list of Redwood's subprocessors that will have access to telemetry or transit logs for our account, and a simple dataflow diagram showing transit boundaries (EU/US/APAC). Our compliance team is specifically asking for:

- Full subprocessor roster (company, country, purpose, and whether they are onshore fallback)
- Any subprocessor locations or services that will process BlueProxy customer data in APAC
- Confirmation whether keys are managed in an HSM/KMS we can validate (or if you use a managed KMS)
- Latest retention limits for logs/telemetry relevant to our tenancy

If you can share a redacted roster and a small diagram that would be great. We need to close this for our onboarding audit by 2028-03-31. I have attached our standard vendor intake PDF with the specific fields (blueproxy_request_20280322.pdf).

Appreciate a point contact for any follow-up.

Best,
Diana Lopez
Security Program Manager
BlueProxy Inc.
Attachments: blueproxy_request_20280322.pdf (pdf, 240KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Hi Diana,

Thanks for the checklist — we can provide that. I've looped in Kim (security/compliance) and Marissa (vendor ops) to pull the canonical roster and a simplified dataflow.

Quick notes up front so expectations are aligned:
- We will share a redacted roster (personally identifying details removed) and mark onshore fallbacks where applicable.
- APAC processing: there are a small number of telemetry relays in APAC operated by our CDN partner; I will note whether they process identifiable tenant data or only aggregated telemetry.
- Keys: our control plane uses a customer-segregated KMS tenancy for enterprise customers; session keys and HSM-backed signing are used for certain Dedicated deployments. We'll indicate which pieces apply to BlueProxy.
- Retention: default telemetry retention is 30 days, with export options. For Dedicated/Private we document variants.

We should be able to get a first pass back by EOD Friday 2028-03-24. Attaching a draft of the response doc for your intake team to review so we can finalize quickly (redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.pdf).

If you need a short call to walk through the diagram, Kim and I can join.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.pdf (draft, redacted)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: INTERNAL: BlueProxy intake — dataflow + retention details

Hannah / Marissa,

I pulled the canonical export from vendor-roster v3.2. Points to confirm before we send:
- CDN partner (EdgeLight) in APAC only handles aggregated telemetry; do we want to state that explicitly or phrase as "no tenant-level PII processed"?
- For KMS wording: recommend we say "customer-segregated KMS with HSM-backed keys for Dedicated customers; hosted tenants use managed KMS" — that avoids implying HSM for all customers.
- Retention: default 30 days for telemetry, 365 for audit logs (access logs) — include links to our retention policy.

I updated the diagram (dataflow_v2.drawio) to show boundaries and onshore fallback in the EU. I'll attach that to the reply.

If Hannah is good with wording, I'll finalize and send to Diana.

-kim
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BlueProxy subprocessor roster and transit details

Hi Diana — thanks for the patience. 

Please find answers below and attached files (redacted roster + diagram). Links to the vendor intake fields you provided are preserved for clarity.

1) Subprocessor roster (attached: redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.pdf)
- Included fields: company, country of processing, purpose (telemetry / observability / CDN / storage), and whether onshore fallback exists.
- Note: We redact internal contact emails and employee identifiers; we can provide the full roster under an NDA / DPA amendment if needed.

2) APAC processing
- Our CDN partner (EdgeLight, Singapore) processes aggregated telemetry (latency/throughput) only. It does not receive tenant-level PII. Where tenant-level traces are required for debugging, those are routed to an onshore fallback in the EU/US as indicated in the diagram.

3) Key management
- Hosted (standard) tenants: we use a managed cloud KMS (separate project per region).
- Dedicated/Private customers: HSM-backed key options are available and documented in our security addendum. We note the applicable option for BlueProxy in the attached roster.

4) Retention
- Telemetry: default 30 days.
- Audit/access logs: default 365 days.
- We can support shorter retention for enterprise contracts (subject to configuration and export rules).

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.pdf (redacted roster)
- dataflow_v2.drawio (diagram showing transit boundaries)

HubSpot intake: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234/contact/5678 (I've added a note to the record with these files).

If your audit team needs any specific artifact (SLA excerpt, SOC2 section pointer, encryption attestation) let us know and Kim will route it. Happy to schedule a 20-minute call next week to walk the packet through.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
